name: INA326EA_2K5
title: Instrumentation amplifier with rail-to-rail inputs and output, precision auto-corrected (INA326; INA327 adds shutdown)
summary: The INA326 and INA327 are single-supply instrumentation amplifiers whose inputs work from 20 mV below the negative rail to 100 mV above the positive rail and whose output reaches within 10 mV of either rail. Internal auto-correction keeps offset at 100 µV maximum and drift at 0.4 µV/°C maximum, with almost no 1/f noise. Two resistors set the gain, G = 2 × R2 / R1, from below 0.1 to above 10000; two capacitors filter the auto-correction ripple and set the bandwidth. The INA327 adds an Enable pin; the INA326 comes in MSOP-8 and the INA327 in MSOP-10, both for +2.7 V to +5.5 V.
key_figures: 33 nV/√Hz at G = 100; 0.8 µVp-p 0.01 Hz to 10 Hz
+2.7 V to +5.5 V, 2.4 mA typ; 2 µA typ shut down (INA327)

circuits.title: Basic connections, ±2.5 V supplies
circuits.description: The INA326 on split ±2.5 V rails. R1 between pins 1 and 8 and R2 from pin 5 to the reference ground set the gain, G = 2 × R2 / R1; C2 across R2 and the 100 Ω / 1 µF RO-CO pair on the output each give a pole near 1.5 kHz, together a two-pole roll-off that is 3 dB down at 1 kHz and that strips the auto-correction ripple. The output is measured against IACOMMON, the low end of R2. One 0.1 µF capacitor bridges V+ to V−. Values shown are the G = 100 row of the dual-supply gain table; other gains take their R1, R2 and C2 from that table.

circuits.title: Basic connections, single +5 V supply
circuits.description: The same gain and filter network on one positive rail, V− at ground. On a single supply R2 is taken larger (200 kΩ in this circuit) so the output can reach the rails while the current in R2 stays within ±25 µA; that raises the input-referred offset. A reading close to 0 V needs a small output offset (see the output-offset circuit). Values shown are the G = 100 row of the single-supply gain table.

circuits.title: Input bias current return path
circuits.description: A floating thermocouple across the two inputs, with a resistor from VIN+ to ground so both input bias currents have somewhere to go; without it the inputs drift to an undefined voltage. Gain resistors and the output filter are as in the basic connection.

circuits.title: Generating an output offset voltage
circuits.description: R2 to ground and R′2 to VREF form a divider at pin 5, so the output sits at a small positive offset (100 mV, say) with zero input; a single-supply circuit can then read signals at and near zero. The gain uses R2 and R′2 in parallel: G = 2 (R2 ∥ R′2) / R1. C2 from pin 5 to ground and R0-C0 on the output are the usual filters.

circuits.title: Bridge amplifier with output referred to VREF/2
circuits.description: A resistor bridge excited from VREF feeds the inputs, and two 200 kΩ resistors from VREF to ground set the R2 node at VREF/2, so the output idles at half the reference. The A/D converter takes the same VREF as its reference. The parallel 200 kΩ pair gives G = 2 (200 kΩ ∥ 200 kΩ) / 2 kΩ = 100. RO-CO (100 Ω, 1 µF) filters the output into the converter.

circuits.title: High-side current shunt measurement
circuits.description: A shunt RS between the +5 V rail and a load; VIN+ reaches the supply end through 2 kΩ and VIN− sits on the load end. VO = 2 (IL × RS) R2 / R1. With V+ (pin 7) on the load side of the shunt, the INA326's own supply current is part of the measured current; tied straight to +5 V instead, it is left out. RS must be small enough that the inputs stay within 100 mV above the rail. A near-zero reading needs an output offset (the output-offset circuit).
notes: Pin 7 at the load end of RS counts the quiescent current in the measurement; pin 7 at +5 V does not.

circuits.title: Low-side current shunt measurement
circuits.description: The shunt RS sits between the load's return and ground. VIN+ connects to the load end of RS and VIN− returns to ground through 2 kΩ. VO = 2 (IL × RS) R2 / R1. With V− (pin 4) on the load end of the shunt the quiescent current is measured with the load; tied to ground directly it is not. RS must keep the inputs within 20 mV below the rail. A reading near zero needs an output offset.
notes: Pin 4 at the load end of RS counts the quiescent current in the measurement; pin 4 at ground does not.

circuits.title: Low-side −48 V current shunt monitor
circuits.description: The INA326 floats on the −48 V rail: a ZMM5231B 5.1 V zener fed from ground through 8.45 kΩ makes its supply (pin 7 to pin 4), bypassed by 0.1 µF. The shunt voltage across RS (0 to 50 mV) is amplified as a current out of pin 5, which a ZVN4525G high-voltage n-channel FET, gate on the zener rail, carries up through RSTART (100 kΩ) to the summing node of an OPA336 on +5 V. RF (100 kΩ with 1 nF) turns that current into VO = 2 (IL × RS) RF / RI, with RI = 2 kΩ; RPULL-DOWN (200 kΩ) runs from VO to −48 V. Accuracy is 0.2 %; with a suitable high-voltage FET the same circuit works from a −250 V supply.
notes: 0.2 % accuracy.
With a suitable high-voltage FET the circuit can be built for a −250 V supply.

circuits.title: High-side +48 V current shunt monitor
circuits.description: The mirror of the −48 V monitor for a high-side shunt. The INA326 hangs from +48 V: pin 7 on the rail, pin 4 on a node held 5.1 V below it by a ZMM5231B zener with 8.45 kΩ to ground and 0.1 µF across. RSHUNT (0 to 50 mV) sits between +48 V and the load, with VIN+ on the rail and VIN− on the load side; RI = 2 kΩ. The current from pin 5 passes through a ZVP4525 high-voltage p-channel FET, gate on the floating ground, into 75 kΩ ∥ 1 nF to ground. An OPA336 on +5 V with 49.9 kΩ feedback and 165 kΩ to ground amplifies that voltage to VO = 0.1 V to 4.9 V.

circuits.title: Output offset adjustment from a DAC
circuits.description: The low end of R2 (100 kΩ, with 1 nF across) goes to a DAC output instead of ground, so the output follows the DAC: VO = VIN × 100 + VDAC, with VDAC from 0.075 V to 4.925 V. R1 = 2 kΩ gives G = 100.
notes: The terminal marked + goes to pin 2 and the terminal marked − to pin 3.

circuits.title: Multiplexed output
circuits.description: Three INA327s on +5 V with their outputs tied to one VO line. Logic powered from 1.8 V to 5 V drives each Enable pin; only the enabled amplifier drives the line, since a disabled INA327's output goes high-impedance. Each has its own gain resistor and a 1 nF capacitor on its R2 node; the three R2 resistors may be one shared resistor.

circuits.title: Output taken from pin 5 to swing past the rail
circuits.description: The INA326 output buffer (pin 6) is left open and the signal is taken at pin 5, where the internal charge pumps let R2's voltage swing from about −20 mV to 100 mV above +5 V. An OPA277 follower on ±15 V buffers that node to VO. The source VD rides on a common-mode voltage VCM.
notes: Pin 5 typically swings from −20 mV to (+5 V + 100 mV).

circuits.title: Programmable ±25 µA current source with high output resistance
circuits.description: A DAC (0 to 5 V) drives VIN− and VIN+ sits at VREF = +2.5 V across R1 = 200 kΩ, so the current out of pin 5 is IOUT = (VREF − VDAC) / R1 ± 50 nA, up to ±25 µA. CF from pin 5 to ground (1 nF to 1 µF) filters it, and the current leaves through RF = 10 kΩ. Output resistance is typically 800 MΩ and resolution better than 5 nA. Pin 6 is not used.
notes: Output resistance is typically 800 MΩ; resolution is under 5 nA.

circuits.title: Programmable ±5 mA current source
circuits.description: On ±2.5 V supplies the DAC output drives VIN− against VIN+ at VREF = +2.5 V, with RI = 200 kΩ. Pin 5 feeds the output node through 10 kΩ and pin 6 through 49.9 Ω, so the output buffer supplies the current scaled up by the resistor ratio: IOUT = 2 ((VREF − VDAC) / 200 kΩ) (1 + 10 kΩ / 49.9 Ω). A 0.1 µF capacitor from the output node to ground filters it. IO reaches ±5 mA with 0.1 µA stability.
notes: IO = ±5 mA with 0.1 µA stability.

circuits.title: ±27 V, 200 mA amplifier with 100 µV offset
circuits.description: An OPA551 (a 60 V op amp on ±30 V) is an inverting amplifier with RI = 1 kΩ and RF = 100 kΩ, G = −RF / RI = −100 V/V. The INA326 on +5 V watches the OPA551's inverting input through 20 kΩ against ground and drives its non-inverting input from pin 5 (1 MΩ ∥ 10 nF to ground) through 20 kΩ, nulling the OPA551's offset to 100 µV (VOS = −100 µV at 200 mA, VO = −27 V). The INA326's charge pump lets pin 5 go 20 mV below ground, so negative offsets are corrected without a negative supply. The OPA551's bias current, 100 pA, through 2 kΩ adds 0.2 µV.
notes: The OPA551 is a 60 V op amp.
Negative OPA551 offsets are corrected without any negative supply.
The OPA551 bias current adds 100 pA × 2 kΩ = 0.2 µV of offset.

circuits.title: Single-supply PID temperature control loop
circuits.description: A thermoelectric-cooler controller on one +5 V supply. A REF1004-2.5 (D1, fed by R10 1 kΩ, filtered by R13 20 Ω and C6 10 µF) supplies 2.5 V to a 10 kΩ thermistor with R12 15 kΩ, and to a set-point divider R11 14.3 kΩ, R7 1 kΩ pot and R6 9.53 kΩ. The INA326 (R9 2 kΩ, R8 100 kΩ ∥ C5 1 nF to VBIAS, gain 100 V/V) amplifies the difference between thermistor and set point. R14 10 kΩ with C7 22 nF filters it into an OPA4340 section whose gain is set by R18 10 kΩ against R15 200 Ω plus the R16 2 kΩ loop-gain pot. That error drives three OPA4340 sections in parallel: an integrator (R17 5 kΩ pot, RINT 10 MΩ, CINT 1 µF; time constant 1 s to 10 s), a proportional stage (R19 and R1, both 100 kΩ) and a differentiator (R20 5 kΩ pot, CDIFF 1 µF, R2 100 kΩ, RDIFF 1 MΩ; 100 ms to 1 s). An OPA2340 half sums them through R21, R22 and R23 (10 kΩ each) with R25 10 kΩ ∥ C8 0.1 µF feedback to the output for the TEC driver. The other OPA2340 half buffers a mid-supply VBIAS from R5 and R4 (20 kΩ each) with C2 470 nF. All stages work about VBIAS.

operation.text: The input amplifiers A1 and A2 force the differential input voltage across R1. A2 adds the R1 current to a mirrored copy of A1's, so twice the R1 current flows out of (or into) pin 5 and through R2, giving G = 2 × R2 / R1. A3 buffers the R2 voltage to the output. Common-mode and supply rejection come from this current-mode processing rather than from matched resistors, so resistance in the reference connection or a socket does not degrade CMR. Internal charge pumps supply A1, A2, their mirrors and A3's input stage from beyond both rails, which is why pin 5 and the inputs reach 20 mV below V− and 100 mV above V+.

An internal oscillator at 90 kHz (±20 %) runs the auto-correction that removes offset and almost all 1/f noise at gains of 100 and above. It leaves ripple at about 90 kHz and its harmonics, which the C2 and CO filters remove; lower cutoff gives less noise. Spurs can be cut further by filtering below 1 kHz. At gains below 10 the output stage still shows some 1/f noise.

C2 across R2 and the RO-CO pair on the output each make a pole; with both at 1.5 kHz the response is two-pole and −3 dB at 1 kHz, which is why bandwidth is nearly the same at every gain. Both poles are usually set to the same frequency. Filtering sets slew rate, settling and overload recovery. RO is kept low so a following load does not make a gain error, which pushes CO up; RO-CO can be scaled to a higher impedance when the load is very light. The output filter can double as the anti-alias filter for an A/D converter and may be left off where less precision is needed. Not enough filtering at pin 5 makes ripple peaks hit the rail on large swings and shifts the average, a nonlinearity.

For settling to 0.01 %, some capacitors above 0.1 µF show dielectric absorption that lengthens settling. Polypropylene, polystyrene and polycarbonate are good choices; some high-K ceramics leave slow settling tails, though not at the 0.1 % level. Electrolytic capacitors are not for C2 or CO.

R2 values in the gain tables keep the current into R2 within ±25 µA with R1 at 2 kΩ or more. A lower R2 lowers input-referred offset and drift, and suits circuits with small swing or low supply voltage. A single supply with R2 to ground needs a larger R2 to stay under 25 µA, raising offset and drift. More than 25 µA in R2 does no damage but can add nonlinearity. Dual-supply and single-supply circuits use different best values.

Input impedance is about 10^10 Ω and bias current about ±0.2 nA, nearly independent of input voltage. Both inputs still need a DC path for that current; a floating source such as a thermocouple needs a resistor to ground on one input, or the inputs drift and the output is invalid.
Each input is linear from 20 mV below the negative rail to 100 mV above the positive rail.

Internal diodes clamp each input to the rails. If an input can go more than 0.5 V past a supply, its current must be held under 10 mA, usually with a series resistor; a source that limits its own current needs none.
The output is referred to IACOMMON, the low end of R2. Lifting IACOMMON, by a divider to a reference or by a DAC, offsets the output; a single-supply circuit needs such an offset to read near zero.

A logic high on Enable turns the amplifier on and a logic low turns it off, cutting supply current from 2.4 mA to about 2 µA. Turn-on takes 75 µs plus the filter's settling; turn-off takes 100 µs. Disabled, the output is high impedance, so several INA327 outputs can share a bus or the part can be run as a gated amplifier. The pin is a CMOS input and must be driven or tied, not left open. Pin 5 of the INA327 must go to V+. The INA327 pin numbers differ from the INA326.
Capacitance at the R1 pins (1 and 8) limits high-frequency CMR, so keep it small. A 0.1 µF bypass belongs directly across V+ and V− (pins 7 and 4), close to the part, on split supplies too.
